# Review

Outline. Shared by the Builder and the Reviewer. The tier criteria, sensitive-path floors,
finding categories, their mapping and the tier challenge live in `AGENTS.md`'s Code Review
Rules, which the review bots also read; this file says how they are applied.

## Setting the tier

- The change sets the tier, not the ticket or the author.
- The Builder writes `Risk: <tier> — <reason>`, the only record of the tier.
- Others only raise it: the self-verification subagent, a review bot's tier challenge, the
  Reviewer. The Builder updates the line.
- Only habit lowers it, in a PR comment the Builder records. Not below a sensitive path's
  floor; the gate enforces that for everyone.
- A raised tier applies to the current head; reviews run under the lower tier don't count.
- A confirmed pure revert is low (`builder.md`).

## Minimum reviews

| | low | medium | high |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Self-verification | yes | yes | yes |
| Reviewer session | — | yes | yes, different vendor from the Builder |
| Review bots | Bugbot | Bugbot | Bugbot and the Codex review bot |
| Security review | — | — | when the reason involves authentication, privacy or secrets |
| Merge summary by | Builder | Reviewer | Reviewer, as the high-risk report |

- The kinds don't substitute for each other. Minimums are floors; every review that runs
  binds.
- High adds: plain-language before-and-after evidence; one-way doors rehearsed on a copy
  with the result attached; every finding answered, Nits included; only the high part in
  the PR; habit's go-ahead after merge for each one-way-door step (`builder.md`, After
  merge).

## Review bots

- Bugbot: the Builder requests it on every head that needs review.
- The Codex review bot: only habit's request works (`builder.md`, The Reviewer handoff).
- Only a request comment writes a bot's trigger; other text names the bot.
- Review state per head: clear, flagged or unavailable. Codex's from its
  `codex-review-state` marker on the head; Bugbot's from its check, with `neutral`
  inspected, never read as success.
- Unavailable: no result 30 minutes after the request, an error or no quota. Request once
  more. Still unavailable: low and medium escalate with the Codex request as substitute;
  high escalates, and habit waits or accepts one bot fewer, recorded in the report.

## Answering findings

- Important: fix it ("Fixed in `<sha>`") or reject it with evidence, a command and its
  output or a concrete fact ("Not fixing: …"); then resolve the thread.
  - Medium and high: the Reviewer judges each rejection.
  - Low: rejecting a bot's Important raises the PR to medium.
- Nit: optional at low and medium; at high, reply to each.
- Pre-existing: never blocks. Important-severity ones go into one `needs-triage` issue per
  PR, linked from the merge summary.

## Rounds

- A round: every required review ran on one head, and the Builder responded.
- Cap: three. An Important still open after round 3: the Builder escalates with the options
  (change approach, split, more rounds, drop).
- Any new head, a sync included, gets the bots again and a Reviewer pass over the change.
  The Builder reruns verification and updates the evidence comment.
- Waiting: the Builder and the Reviewer wait for each other on the PR in their harness. One
  that can't wait stops and says what it waits for; habit says "continue" there.

## Subagents and the security review

- Self-verification (`builder.md`, step 6) and the security review each run as a subagent
  with no conversation context, named as such in its task.
- Security review: outline of the checks (authentication paths, secret handling, input
  trust, privacy exposure), rated HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW.

## Merge summary and high-risk report

- Written by: the Builder at low, the Reviewer at medium and high, after the last clear
  review.
- First confirm, on the head it names: each required review ran and is clear; the Gate and
  Merge rulesets' rules are in effect. If not in effect, tell habit in Chinese with the
  remedies, and still hand over the command.
- On the PR, in English: one comment titled "Merge summary", the tier and the short head
  SHA. A new head makes it stale.
- In the terminal, in Chinese:
  - First line: tier, verdict, Important / Nit / Pre-existing counts.
  - Seven items: tier and why; what changed in 3–5 plain bullets; each acceptance
    criterion met or not; evidence in plain words; each reviewer's findings and answers;
    what the checks don't cover; how to revert.
  - High-risk report adds: why high; the rehearsal result; each step awaiting habit's
    go-ahead, what it does, and whether it can be undone.
  - Then the pinned merge command, which habit runs through habit's own account alias:
    `ghm pr merge <n> --admin --squash --match-head-commit <sha>`.
  - Then one start instruction for the next ticket this merge unblocks, if any.
- No code locations, in either copy.
